[2025-07-10 15:58] talonflame1 : <@1364429602117914685> I would say figure out how you best want to enjoy your time on the game. What might be the logically best thing for you to do may also be incredibly boring and have you lose interest in the game before it pays off.   If you want to win games as fast as possible, then do so. Obviously there are better contracts out there than others. Try to look at teams in 1.1 as a template of what could be good players, contracts, etc. Since you're not exactly attached to your spawn guys, feel free to make trades for players you think will be good.  Or if you want to tank, then tank. Trade your pro players with value for futures and build through young prospects. Sure, a few seasons will be boring with nothing to play for, but you'll be rewarded hopefully with some good young talent.  There's no right answer. Do what makes the game fun for you and over time you'll move up to the top league.

The offer by a different GM that passed the board was at least better although still not very exciting.  <@869928525199720508> Reason the board is not fixed is to try and prevent group thinking and user bias. Although with the expanded board (up to  21 members) there is already a decent chance of returning members from season-to-season. Ideally the expected outcome filters some of the noise (misclicks, blindly accepting any offer, user bias) and this is looked at. Data shows that the board is more likely to give the benefit of the doubt when it comes to approving trade offers. That's something users wished for in the past and a healthy thing to have. At the same time there have been approved trades where the expected outcome clearly should have been a rejection. I've also seen a few rejected trades that seemed fine and within limits, but these are rare luckily.

[2025-08-13 23:04] chimkintendies : What's in a pick?  Okay so I was curious. A common question I have is what kind of player should I expect with a certain draft pick in return. It's a question we all ask, especially if you've been on the trade board in the past. Though analyzing every league would be tedious and digging deeper than overalls would take ages, I looked back at previous 1.1 draft selections and how they turned out. Here are my findings: - Round 1 picks tend to end in the 70s on average, with the top 10 selections maxing near the mid-70s. You'll also find a few 80s in most drafts. There's a decent chance you get an 80 if you pick in the top 5... with a little bit of luck. - Round 2 picks end up falling in the 60s at their true potential. There are a handful of 70s mixed in there as well. - Round 3 picks give you a mid-50s player. About 25% or so will get a player that hits 60. - Round 4 picks will rarely reach the 60s. At their best, players could creep into the mid-50s. A couple from each draft may end up at 60. - Round 5 players, at least in 1.1, will almost always peak below 55.

[2025-12-03 17:01] beanz6969 : Is “expected goals” completely useless?
[2025-12-03 17:01] d0ghouse : What makes you think that?
[2025-12-03 17:04] beanz6969 : It’s almost always wrong. I am Seeing that the winning team regularly has less expected goals.
[2025-12-03 17:22] d0ghouse : The margins are close since the average save% is around 90% all things being equal (1 in 10 shots is a goal). But the majority of games should definitely be won by teams that had the higher expected goals in a match. It's a good indicator if your team performed up their standards or not (dGF+dSV). If a team is still winning despite these being in the negative they are a very strong team. It can help you decide if you need to make adjustments or if the team just had a bad streak.

[2025-12-08 11:55] talonflame1 : It's probably because people don't really know how to value picks.   One way to view them is the way you just outlined. A late 1st is usually a low 60 overall player. Especially in 1.1 and other leagues that are filled with real people and not bots. The problem with this is that how does anyone over a 70 get traded? For example, if we are going by min overall per round it's usually something like this:  <50 min - 5th low 50 min - 4th mid 50 min - 3rd high 50 min - 2nd 60-65 min - late 1st 66-72 - early 1st 73-91 - ?????  The problem with the model is when it comes to players in the 70-80s. How do you rate how many additional picks would be required?  The other model would be based on pro rosters:  40s to low 50 - 5th but likely no value Fourth liner (55-60) - 4th Third liner (60-67) - 3rd Second liner (68-74) - 2nd First line (75-82) - 1st  This model is more inclusive to every player in the game. The issue relates to dealing with age. In this model, a newly drafted 18 year old in the late first round now at a min 63 let's say would now only be worth a 3rd. Why is this player worth a late first rounder on day 62, but the second he's drafted his value shoots down to a third? Same on the upper end, since a 20 year old 80 overall is worth more than a 30 year old 80 overall.
[2025-12-08 11:59] talonflame1 : So take your trade for example.  Two players at low 60 min overalls for a late first.  In the first model, you're essentially trading two players worth a late first for one late first pick, which would explain the vote saying Racers are favored  In the second model, you're essentially trading two players worth third round picks for a first round pick, which would explain why you are being favored.

[2026-01-08 10:34] talonflame1 : The trade doesn't follow the structure of a cap dump as defined throughout the seasons of this game.  Cap dumps are defined by having an untradeable asset or being over the cap. The structure of a cap dump deal is:   Team with money gives up literally nothing (5th round pick / trash Frm or u21 player)  Team looking to dump gives up the dumped player + picks/Player = to the amount of cap being taken on. Generally, under 2 mil is a 3rd, 3-4 mil is a 2nd, and 5+ is a 1st. Amount of seasons left on the dumped player's deal also is taken to account.  If your deal is a cap dump, your trade partner's 4th is too high, and you are not providing compensation (in this case a 2nd round pick or equivalent prospect). Guarenteed a deal of this structure will go through.  If your deal is a straight up trade, the other team would have to pay more and comments need to be clear from both people that this is a hockey deal and not a cap dump.

[2026-04-04 07:34] bowmoore : Hi guys, I am new to this game. 🙂 What would you say are the 3 most important skills for Forwards Defenders Goalies ?
[2026-04-04 07:48] talonflame1 : For goalies: END tells you how many games they can play before tired. Generally your starter should be at 7+ for END.   STK is used the least, so if you want a bad stat, that would be the one.
[2026-04-04 07:55] talonflame1 : TLDR for skaters:  SHO and PAS directly related to scoring  SKA and PWR relate to actually having the puck  CHK and DEF relate to defending, where as DSC relates to how much penalties you take  FAF you only need one good face off guy per line. Doesn’t have to be the center.   Endurance breakpoints: Line 1:7+, L2: 6+, D pair 1: 8+, Dpair 2: 6+  You can have a player with less endurance play on higher lines, but ultimately it’s dimishing returns
[2026-04-04 07:56] elitesteel : Steelers goalies are famous for having no endurance. Guess we've figured out why my team is always so bad 😆
[2026-04-04 07:58] talonflame1 : Haha endurance also tells you how much condition you get back between periods. So if your goalie is making many saves with low endurance, he’ll be like 60% of themselves by period 3

[2026-04-14 17:42] talonflame1 : What I’ve been working with has been going off min values:  80s - 1st+ Mid to high 70- 1st High 60 to Low 70 - 2nd Low to mid 60 - 3rd 55-60 min - 4th <55 min - 5th  Go up or down a tier if one of the following is true (generally does not stack):  Specials - Up 18-20 and uncapped for the most part - Up Age 35+ - Down Expiring contract in TW2 - Down unless extension is already signed Currently over the cap (for a hockey trade not dump) - Down Elite goalie - Up Non Pro Starting goalie - Down  Draft pick trades in TW1 follow these rules:  Two 5th = 4th Two 4th = 3rd Two 3rd = 2nd Two 2nd = 1st  In TW2 draft picks gain or lose value based on the following:  Unscouted draft - down High round picks (1-10, 21-30, etc) - Up  Cap dumps reserved for players on bad deals that no one wants. Starting framework is a 5th (or Garbage Prospect) on the team receiving the dump. Team dumping includes the TOTAL salary dumped + compensation  <1 mil salary dumped - 4th 1-2 mil dumped - 3rd 2-4.5 mil dumped - 2nd 4.5-7 mil dumped - 2nd + 3rd 7-10 mil dumped - 1st 10+ mil dumped - 1st+

[2026-04-22 14:31] c0ntrail : In short, timezones.
[2026-04-22 14:32] c0ntrail : When you have teams on the east coast usa and in Melbourne Australia the daily flip happens at odd local times. Delaying it to give teams an entire waking day to manage the repercussions of a trade makes it easier for those in disparate time zones.

[2026-04-22 15:28] d0ghouse : "This is for 2 reasons. First one is to give some time to trade board to analyse the trade. The board has 24 hours.  Second reason is to ensure that the listed projected salary changes do not depend on the time of approval by board. For instance, suppose GM accepted a trade 1 hour before the daily update and board approved it just before the daily update. In this case there is only 1 salary day in play instead of the 2 that were used in the calculated projected salary change. Hence, trades always take place on the second daily update after the trade was accepted by the GM." - HNAdmin Source: https://discord.com/channels/922093338595831808/922093338595831811/948129338304364544
[2026-04-22 15:43] hnadmin : Regarding contract talks: I’m working on an update that makes agents respond instantly when GMs **start** contract talks. This means response time will only be in effect during renegotiations. It also means that contract talks will no longer be copied after a trade, but will be deleted instead. Talks are currently copied to give GMs enough time to sign traded players, but with instant responses at the start, this is no longer necessary.

There's only so much development time available and everyone is able to reach their full potential with daily training. So it's worth it to keep an eye on the daily training log (all other factors considered equal such as age, skill level and coaching boost).

If you want any kind of skill progression, you'll have to track it externally.

[2026-08-25 09:02] talonflame1 : I think the pain points of coaching are:  There is no cost to acquire or maintain your coaches. Once they are yours, they remain yours til they retire.   The method of acquiring a coach is luck of the draw. There is no way of increasing your odds of acquiring a coach between offers of the same position.   The development of new coaches is semi exclusive and faces the same issue as high value coaches. Longer standing franchises are more likely to have returning players as pipeline for developing coaches. Newer franchises have a harder time of breaking into coaching market without this advantage. Their only option is to hit the Market.   In addition, getting a high value developing coaches requires you many times to offer a higher position than that coach deserves. That leads to tanking and praying that the coaches develops fast.   Having good coaches affects your team’s success too much. Dynasties feel impossible to stop once the super coaching staff is acquired.

[2026-09-19 09:35] mikikuba : I have a question: when 17-year-old players move up from the U17 squad to the U21 team at the end of the season, who replaces them? Will the squad be automatically replenished with new players, or will I have to draft new young players (aged 15, 16, and 17) to keep the U17 roster full?
[2026-09-19 09:45] hnadmin : Your U17 will automatically be replenished with 7 new 15-year-old players. Five of them will be a draftee in 3 seasons, while the other two will not be draft-eligible and join your U21 in 3 seasons.
[2026-09-19 09:47] hnadmin : One of those 2 not-draft eligible players is the import player you picked in the Import Draft
[2026-09-19 09:50] mikikuba : Great, thanks for the answer. Will their positions be chosen randomly, or can I select the specific players I need—for example, RW or LD?
[2026-09-19 09:50] mikikuba : when and how i will picked this player ?
[2026-09-19 09:51] mikikuba : i see
[2026-09-19 09:52] hnadmin : Those 6 new players will get a position so that your U17 can fill a lineup. Your U17 won't miss players on any position.
[2026-09-19 09:54] hnadmin : So basically, you get to pick one player, and the other 6 will be assigned a position so that your U17 is not short on any position. For example, if you are missing a goalie, you will get a goalie.

[2026-09-26 11:23] mikikuba : Regarding in-game instructions: what is the difference between the "any score" and "equel score" settings? If I have an instruction set for position 8—"trailing by 1 goal"—will that instruction work and override the "any score" one?
[2026-09-26 12:33] _pignon_ : The last valid instruction will apply. Any score - always applies; Trailing by 1 - applies if you are behind exactly 1 goal.
[2026-09-26 12:34] _pignon_ : Equal score - applies when both team have the same number of goals.
[2026-09-26 12:36] mikikuba : Any score always applies and what if i am losing by one goal , so it is comes into effect trailing by one goal?
[2026-09-26 12:37] mikikuba : or stay instructions Any score ?
[2026-09-26 12:37] mikikuba : How are the instructions prioritized—does the highest one take precedence?
[2026-09-26 12:39] _pignon_ : As I said the last valid instruction applies. So if your Trailing instruction is after your Any score then the Trailing one overrides the Any score one.
[2026-09-26 12:39] _pignon_ : *When you are behind by 1.
[2026-09-26 12:42] _pignon_ : So if you put Any score instruction at the bottom, it will always apply. (for the selected lines)
[2026-09-26 12:43] _pignon_ : Since there is nothing lower after it to override it.
[2026-09-26 12:43] mikikuba : Okay, I understand it better now—thank you.
[2026-09-26 12:43] mikikuba : 🙂
[2026-09-26 12:44] _pignon_ : You are welcome.

Selling a player in his contract year for max value is an unrealistic pipe dream, and so is waiting until the player is 35 to move him.  You have to assume some risk when you milk every year out of a team friendly contract and then when he’s about to get paid flip him and get offended that someone doesn’t want to pay the new contract and pay the value attached to him.  I’ve had people get mad because I’ve devalued a guy that’s going from a 2m a year contract to a 4.5m deal because the value per overall is about to plummet.  So it’s a 2 way street as far as problems go right now
[2023-09-20 19:59] hffo : <#922093338595831811>
[2023-09-20 20:06] talonflame1 : Well yeah thats to be expected. The value is going to go up and down based on age and contract, but the value should never hit 0. It goes both ways; a 70+ OVR guy shouldnt be going for below a 3rd at least, and as the seller you shouldnt continue to resign a guy that you dont want and has no value.   The issue lies in the fact that while one is actively hurting the game and the other is just people getting mad over unrealistic expectations. If no one is interested in paying a reasonable price for a player, just let the player go at the end of the contract, wait for a better offer (in the case of longer contracts), or buy the guy out. The trade board is here to determine fair value. Sure, a side can win a trade, but when the value is completely unbalanced it should be vetoed.
